summary: When a woman loses a pregnancy very early and only a small piece comes out, is she tamei? The Tanna Kamma and Rabbi Yehudah argue.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a piece,
chunks.explain: A woman who lost a pregnancy very early.
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who discharges an amorphous piece

chunks.en: if there is blood with it,
chunks.st: of tissue, if there is blood that emerges with it,

chunks.en: she is tamei.
chunks.st: the woman is ritually impure

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: with the impurity of a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: she is tahor.
chunks.st: And if not, she is pure,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: as she is neither a menstruating woman nor a woman after childbirth. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: either way, she is tamei.
chunks.st: In both this case, where blood emerged, and that case, where no blood emerged, the woman is impure
chunks.stMore: with the impurity of a menstruating woman, as there was certainly undetected blood that emerged with the flesh.

summary: This mishnah talks about things that come out of a woman that do not look like a baby, and how we decide if she is tamei and which days she must keep.

chunks.en: A woman who lost something like a peel,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who discharges an item similar to a shell,

chunks.en: like a hair,
chunks.st: or similar to a hair,

chunks.en: like dust,
chunks.st: or similar to soil,

chunks.en: like red gnats,
chunks.st: or similar to mosquitoes, if such items are red,

chunks.en: should put it into water.
chunks.st: she should cast them into water

chunks.en: If they melted away,
chunks.st: to ascertain their nature: If they dissolved,

chunks.en: she is tamei.
chunks.st: it is blood, and the woman is impure with the impurity of a menstruating woman;

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if not,

chunks.en: she is tahor.
chunks.st: she is pure.

chunks.en: A woman who lost something shaped like fish,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who discharges an item similar to fish

chunks.en: grasshoppers, creeping things or crawling things,
chunks.st: or to grasshoppers, repugnant creatures, or creeping animals,

chunks.en: if there is blood with them,
chunks.st: if there is blood that emerges with them,

chunks.en: she is tamei.
chunks.st: the woman is impure with the impurity of a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: And if not,

chunks.en: she is tahor.
chunks.st: she is pure.

chunks.en: A woman who lost something shaped like an animal,
chunks.st: With regard to a woman who discharges

chunks.en: a wild animal or a bird,
chunks.st: tissue in the form of a type of domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, or bird,

chunks.en: whether it is a kind that is not kosher or kosher,
chunks.st: whether it had the form of a non-kosher species or a kosher species, if

chunks.en: if it is a boy,
chunks.st: it was a male fetus, then she observes
chunks.stMore: the periods of impurity, seven days, and purity, thirty-three days, established in the Torah (see Leviticus 12:2–5)

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy.
chunks.explain: The Torah gives different days after a boy and after a girl.
chunks.st: for a woman who gives birth to a male. And if

chunks.en: And if it is a girl,
chunks.st: the fetus was a female,

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a girl.
chunks.st: the woman observes the periods of impurity, fourteen days, and purity, sixty-six days, established in the Torah for

chunks.en: And if we do not know,
chunks.st: a woman who gives birth to a female. And if the sex of the fetus is unknown, she observes

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
chunks.st: the strictures that apply to a woman who gave birth both to a male and to a female.
chunks.stMore: Accordingly, she is prohibited from engaging in intercourse for fourteen days, but after that, she will be permitted to engage in intercourse despite a discharge of uterine blood until thirty-three days pass after the seven days she would have been prohibited if the fetus were male. The prohibition to enter the Temple will continue until eighty days have passed from the discharge of the fetus. This is

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: Any

chunks.en: anything that does not have a human shape
chunks.st: fetus that is not of human form is not

chunks.en: is not a baby.
chunks.st: regarded as an offspring
chunks.stMore: with regard to observance of these periods, and she is permitted to engage in intercourse provided that she does not experience a discharge of uterine blood.

summary: If what came out was only a sac full of water or other things, it is not a baby. But if it had some shape, she keeps the days for a boy and a girl.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a sac full of water,
chunks.st: A woman who discharges a gestational sac full of fluid,

chunks.en: full of blood,
chunks.st: full of blood,

chunks.en: full of colored things,
chunks.st: or full of different colors

chunks.en: does not need to worry that it was a baby.
chunks.st: need not be concerned that it was an offspring. But if

chunks.en: But if it had a shape,
chunks.st: the sac was one in which tissue developed, her halakhic status is that of a woman after childbirth. Since the sex of the embryo is unknown, the woman observes

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
chunks.st: the strictures of a woman who gave birth both to a male and to a female;
chunks.stMore: she is impure for fourteen days like a woman who gave birth to a female, but blood that she sees thereafter is pure only until forty days after birth, like a woman who gave birth to a male.

summary: This mishnah teaches about other things that come out with a baby, and why a house where they are found becomes tamei.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a flat shape, or an afterbirth,
chunks.st: A woman who discharges a sandal fetus, i.e., one that has the form of a sandal fish, and one who discharges an afterbirth observes

words.note: Shaped like the bottom of a shoe.
What holds the baby before birth.

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
chunks.st: the strictures of a woman who gave birth both to a male and to a female.

chunks.en: If an afterbirth is in the house,
chunks.st: If there is an afterbirth in the house,

chunks.en: the house is tamei.
chunks.st: the house is ritually impure,
chunks.stMore: in the sense that everything under the roof contracts impurity imparted by a corpse. The reason is

chunks.en: Not because the afterbirth is a baby,
chunks.st: not that

chunks.en: but because there is no afterbirth without a baby.
chunks.st: the status of an afterbirth is that of an offspring; rather, it is that there is no afterbirth without an offspring.
chunks.stMore: It is clear that the afterbirth contained an offspring that disintegrated after the miscarriage. That offspring rendered the contents of the house impure.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.stMore: The house does not become a tent over a corpse, as although there had been an offspring in the afterbirth,

chunks.en: the baby melted away before it came out.
chunks.explain: So the house is not tamei.
chunks.st: the offspring disintegrated, turning to blood, before it emerged
chunks.stMore: from the womb, and it was negated by the majority of blood that accompanied the miscarriage.

summary: This mishnah teaches what a woman keeps when we cannot tell if the baby was a boy or a girl, and from when a baby counts as born.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a tumtum,
chunks.st: A woman who discharges or gives birth to a tumtum,

words.note: A baby whose body does not show if it is a boy or a girl.

chunks.en: or an androgynos, keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
chunks.st: whose sexual organs are obscured, or to a hermaphrodite [ve’androginos], who has both male and female sexual organs, shall observe the strictures of a woman who gave birth both to a male and to a female.
chunks.stMore: She is impure for fourteen days like a woman who gave birth to a female, but blood that she sees thereafter is pure only until forty days after birth, like for a woman who gave birth to a male. In a case where she gave birth to twins, if they are

words.note: A baby whose body has signs of both a boy and a girl.

chunks.en: A tumtum and a boy,
chunks.st: a tumtum and a male,

chunks.en: an androgynos and a boy,
chunks.st: or

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
chunks.st: a hermaphrodite and a male, she observes

chunks.en: A tumtum and a girl,
chunks.st: the strictures of a woman who gave birth both to a male and to a female.

chunks.en: an androgynos and a girl,
chunks.st: But if the twins are a tumtum and a female,

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a girl only.
chunks.st: or a hermaphrodite and a female, she shall observe the periods of purity and impurity established by the Torah for a woman who gives birth to a female alone.
chunks.stMore: Regardless of the status of the tumtum and the hermaphrodite, the woman’s seven days of impurity and her succeeding thirty-three days of purity are subsumed in the fourteen days of impurity and sixty-six days of purity for a female. If the fetus

chunks.en: If it came out not whole, or backwards,
chunks.st: emerged in pieces, or

chunks.en: once most of it came out,
chunks.st: if it emerged reversed, i.e., feetfirst rather than headfirst, when most of its

chunks.en: it counts as born.
chunks.st: limbs emerge, its status is like that of a child born,
chunks.stMore: with regard to the impurity of a woman after childbirth. If the fetus

chunks.en: If it came out the normal way,
chunks.st: emerged in

chunks.en: only when most of its head comes out.
chunks.st: the usual manner, headfirst, it is not considered born until most of its head emerges. And what is

chunks.en: And what is most of its head?
chunks.st: considered most of its head?

chunks.en: When its forehead comes out.
chunks.st: It is from when its forehead emerges.

summary: If we do not know what came out, the woman keeps every set of days she might need: for a boy, for a girl, and for a niddah.

chunks.en: A woman who lost something and we do not know what it is,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who discharges and it is not known what is the fetus’s sex, she shall observe

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
chunks.st: the strictures of a woman who gave birth both to a male and to a female.
chunks.stMore: She is impure for fourteen days, like a woman who gave birth to a female, and any blood the woman sees only until forty days after birth, not eighty days thereafter, is pure, like a woman who gave birth to a male. If

chunks.en: If we do not know if it was a baby
chunks.st: it is unknown whether it was a male or female offspring or whether it was not

chunks.en: or not,
chunks.st: an offspring at all, she shall observe the period of impurity for a woman who gave birth to a male and for

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy, for a girl, and for a niddah.
chunks.st: a woman who gave birth to a female; and for any blood that she sees, she observes the halakhot of a menstruating woman.
chunks.stMore: Since it is possible that what she discharged was not an offspring at all, any blood she sees might be due to menstruation, not childbirth.

summary: This mishnah teaches from which day after the pregnancy started something that comes out counts as a baby. Rabbi Yishmael says a boy is formed by day 41 and a girl by day 81; the Sages say both by day 41.

chunks.en: A woman who lost it on the fortieth day
chunks.st: A woman who discharges on the fortieth day

chunks.en: does not need to worry that it was a baby.
chunks.st: since she immersed herself and engaged in intercourse with her husband need not be concerned that it might have been an offspring
chunks.stMore: and she became impure with its miscarriage, as the formation of the offspring in the womb occurs only forty days after conception. But in the case of a woman who discharges

chunks.en: On the forty-first day,
chunks.st: on the forty-first day after immersion, there is concern that perhaps it was an offspring. Since its sex is unknown, she shall observe the period of impurity for

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy, for a girl, and for a niddah.
chunks.st: a woman who gave birth to a male and for

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: a woman who gave birth to a female; and for any blood that she sees, she observes the halakhot of a menstruating woman. Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.en: on day forty-one,
chunks.st: A woman who discharges on the forty-first day

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy and for a niddah.
chunks.st: after immersion observes the seven days of impurity for a woman who gave birth to a male; and for any blood that she sees after seven days, she observes the halakhot of a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: On day eighty-one,
chunks.st: But a woman who discharges on the eighty-first day

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy, for a girl, and for a niddah,
chunks.st: after immersion observes the strictures of a woman who gave birth both to a male and to a female, and

chunks.en: because a boy is finished forming by day forty-one,
chunks.st: also the strictures of a menstruating woman, as the formation of the male offspring concludes on the forty-first

chunks.en: and a girl by day eighty-one.
chunks.st: day and the formation of the female offspring concludes on the eighty-first day.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֶחָד בְּרִיַּת הַזָּכָר וְאֶחָד בְּרִיַּת הַנְּקֵבָה,
chunks.en: both the forming of a boy and the forming of a girl,
chunks.st: With regard to both the formation of the male and the formation of the female, this and that

chunks.en: this one and that one are by day forty-one.
chunks.st: conclude on the forty-first day.
